Platelet Rich Plasma therapy, or PRP, is a treatment option for non-healing muscle and tendon injuries such as those that cause shoulder pain in persons with SCI. Using one's own blood, cells within the blood called "platelets" are concentrated and then re-injected into the muscle and tendon of the shoulder. These platelets release substances known as "growth factors" that lead to tissue healing. By concentrating the platelets we increase the growth factors up to eight times which will promote the healing of tendons. PRP therapy has shown promise in treating tendon and muscle injuries in able-bodied persons. Our combination Joint Injection course is a comprehensive course designed ONLY for medical professionals who wish to offer an exciting new procedure to their aesthetic business.  We only teach a maximum of 2 delegates at any one time, this is to ensure that you gain confidence and competence to be able to leave the training and start treating your own patients immediately. Our PRP Joint Injections training consists of 1 day theory and musculoskeletal assessment and 1-day hands-on practice. If you already have minor injury training, we ask that you send us proof of passing the course this will then allow you to do the 1 day course which will be theory and then practical.  The training course will be carried out by the CMA academy Clinical Director - Susan Langridge and/or Director of Nursing Ferenc Gyalus who have many year’s experience in emergency medicine/surgery. ✨ Myofascial Dry Cupping ✨  Dry cupping is a modality used alongside massage therapy, acupuncture and dry needling which involves the placement of cups onto the skin to create suction.  The aim of dry cupping is to encourage pain relief and healing Dry cupping increases blood circulation to the area where the cups are placed. This can reduce muscle tension, increase range of motion, improve blood flow, promote cell repair and give an overall improvement of wellbeing.  It is generally painless and it is common for dry cupping to leave distinct small circular bruises on the areas where the cups have been placed. MCL - Medial collateral ligament  Media collateral ligament sprains are the most common knee injury.  The MCL is a ligament on the inside of the knee that acts as a stabiliser to prevent valgus stress ( knee caving in ) and rotational forces.  A common cause of a MCL injury is a valgus stress on a stationary knee or sudden forceful turning twisting and cutting.  Signs and Symptoms  * knee giving out * Fluid and blood filling the joint ( severe case) * Painful to touch MCL * MOI - mechanism of injury  Grade 1 tear = no instability of the knee, tenderness on the MCL , few fibres torn. Grade 2 tear = More superficial fibres torn, pain on palpating MCL, tender with no instability.  Grade 3 tear = Complete tear, unstable  Treatment of grade 1-2 * Early rehabilitation  * Weight bearing when pain reduced  * Immobilisation leads to weaker ligaments  * Progressive strength of on hams and quads.  * Favourable long term outcomes  Grade 3 tears are often more complicated and can occur with other ligaments, ACL, PCL and Meniscus, often requiring surgery.  #medialcollateralligamentinjury #PCL #meniscus #injuryrecovery #injuryprevention #physicaltherapy #musculoskeletal #sportrehabilitation #returntoplay

Cervical Radiculopathy (CR) otherwise known as a Pinched cervical nerve   This condition is caused by a compressed cervical spine nerve root.  Symptoms of CR is Pain that radiates down the arm from the neck along the course of the nerve. You may also experience muscle weakness and impaired tendon flexors.  Most frequently caused by disc trauma / herniation and commonly affects younger people in the 3rd and 4th decade.  Disc degeneration increases with age and people in the 5th and 6th decades are affected.  People in the 7th decade of life are likely to  experience CR due to spinal narrowing as a result of cartilage changes.  Treatment of CR -  85% are said to resolve in 8-12 weeks.  Physical therapy consists of gentle ROM exercises, Acupuncture to treat trigger points and ease inflammation, cervical traction and neurodynamics .  When pain is reduced you can work on posture and muscle imbalances with progressive exercises. How to optimise recovery? A big part of your training should be focused on recovery. The better your recovery is, the faster you’re ready to go again! Calf stretching is a crucial component of injury prevention for individuals aged 40 and above. As we age, muscle flexibility tends to decrease, making calf muscles more susceptible to strain and injury. A regular stretching routine can mitigate this risk. Simple exercises like the classic calf stretch, where you lean against a wall with one foot back, can help maintain calf muscle elasticity. These stretches increase blood flow, reduce muscle tightness, and improve range of motion. what is fnd..... Functional neurological disorder (FND) is a condition in which the nervous system doesnt function correctly, causing symptoms without physical  diagnosed disease, such as stroke or Ms But mimicking such symptoms at times for some. It is a problem with the way the brain sends and receives signals to the body.  It can cause a wide variety of symptoms that may cause distress and prevent normal life function. While the symptoms of FND are real and “not just in the persons head,” they often exist without any medical explanation.  It is now widely accepted that FND is a problem based in the functioning of the nervous system that can cause pain, distress and mobility issues.   The cause of FND is not known but it may be triggered by physical,psychological or environmental factors.  There are many symptoms of FND that may be continual or may appear and disappear. Symptoms can continue for some time and hinder an individual’s ability to function as "normal".  Symptoms of FND include:  Limb weakness or paralysis Tremors or abnormal movement (Tics and body jerks)  Problems walking,  Vision and hearing problems  often speech problems, alot suffer  Seizures or loss of consciousness and  Dissociation Problems; Memory or concentration issues,  Tingling/burning of the skin or twitching Fainting or blackouts. extreme Fatigue or sleep problems/insomnia.  Anxiety or depression, Chronic pain Bladder and bowel issues just to name afew more. Symptoms are VERY REAL BEYOND PATIENTS CONTROL! each person may suffer differently to the next due to the complexity of the brain.  #fnd #fndsymptoms #fndawareness #fndhope #musclepain  #Tics #chronicfatigue #stubborn #dontgive #keeptrying #eyepatch #ticynicky

Do you suffer often sufffer from the crippling hidden pains of IBS? Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common disorder that affects the large intestine (colon). While the exact cause of IBS is unknown, it's believed to involve multiple factors including abnormal muscle contractions in the intestines, inflammation, and changes in gut microbiota. The signs and symptoms of IBS can vary widely among individuals, but some hidden signs or less obvious manifestations of IBS may include: Fatigue: Many individuals with IBS report feeling unusually tired, even after a full night's sleep. This fatigue can be related to disrupted sleep patterns due to gastrointestinal symptoms such as pain or diarrhea, or it may be a result of the body's response to chronic stress and discomfort associated with IBS. Joint and Muscle Pain: Some people with IBS may experience joint or muscle pain that seems unrelated to their digestive symptoms. The exact mechanisms behind this are not fully understood, but it may be related to inflammation or changes in immune function associated with IBS. Headaches: Chronic headaches or migraines are reported by some individuals with IBS. Why do my muscles hurt after exercise? If you try a new physical activity, or change your exercise routine, you may experience Delayed-Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS). These muscle aches may come on 6 to 12 hours after a workout and can last from 48 hours and up to 5 days. The pain you experience with DOMS is caused by tiny, microscopic tears in your muscle fibres which your body responds to by increasing inflammation. Medical acupuncture or dry needling consists of the insertion of needles into the skin and the muscle. It has been shown to elicit various benefits, so let’s go through some: -	Pail relief: this is achieved through the stimulation of nociceptors and mechanoreceptors within the tissue which are responsible for detecting painful stimuli. -	Increased blood flow: the needles stimulate vasodilation (dilation of the blood vessels) leading to increased blood flow and oxygenation. -	Local twitch response: when the needle is pulsated (as shown in the video) this causes an involuntary spinal reflex /contraction which can alter the length and tension of muscle fibres -	Increase range of motion: this can occur as a subsequent effect of the increased blood flow and the twitch response. -	Neurophysiological effects: similar to the twitch response, the needle can cause homeostasis at the targeted site which leads to decrease central and peripheral sensitisation to pain. While it is effective in relieving symptoms, like all medications, naproxen can also cause serious side effects, which are important to monitor for safety. ### Serious Side Effects of Naproxen ### If you experience any of the following side effects while taking naproxen, it's crucial to contact your healthcare provider immediately or seek emergency medical help: 1. **Gastrointestinal Issues**:    - Severe indigestion, heartburn, or stomach pains which might be signs of an ulcer or stomach inflammation.    - Vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds; finding blood in your stool or having black, tar-like stools, which can indicate bleeding in the stomach or intestines. 2. **Blood Cell Problems**:    - A frequent sore throat, more frequent nosebleeds, or recurring infections could signal a problem with your blood cells, such as agranulocytosis (a severe reduction in white blood cells). 3. **Anaemia Symptoms**:    - Feelings of faintness, unusual tiredness, or shortness of breath may indicate anaemia, a condition in which you lack enough healthy red blood cells to carry adequate oxygen to your tissues. 4. **Kidney Issues**:    - Signs of kidney damage may include blood in your urine, a decrease in the amount of urine, or persistent nausea and vomiting. 5. **Liver Problems**:    - Yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, which can be a sign of jaundice or liver inflammation. Note that jaundice might be less obvious in individuals with darker skin tones. 6. **Cardiac Conditions**:    - Irregular or unusually slow heartbeats, which could be indicative of high potassium levels in the blood. 7. **Pancreatitis**:    - High fever, severe stomach pain, and vomiting can be signs of pancreatitis, which is inflammation of the pancreas. These side effects are serious and require immediate medical attention to prevent more severe health issues. If you're taking naproxen and begin to notice any of these symptoms, it's crucial to stop taking the medication and consult with a healthcare provider as soon as possible. Our spine is a corridor of energy that is designed to allow us to stand tall, claim our right to be here with upright vigour. Our backs should be both supportive and flexible, like the trunk of a tree. Allowing us to remain standing and weather the external forces that threaten our stability. So what’s the message of back pain? Pain arrives when the flow of energy is interrupted or blocked. And the pain comes on a spectrum between a mild ache and excruciating collapse. Where on the spectrum is your pain? How would you describe it? When muscles tighten they can pull the spine out of alignment creating greater problems. We tighten muscles in defence, in anger and in fear. What has been happening for you recently.. what threatens your stability? What sudden blow has toppled you? What has effected you ability to stand upright with confidence ? Or maybe you’re exhausted and the energy is no longer flowing to support what you’re doing. What are you tired of? What are you frustrated with? The root cause lies in the mind; thoughts and feelings created by the fear of what will happen, or the anger with what didn’t happen causes us to tighten. Pain is the experience of resistance to what is happening or what we believe might happen. The message of healing is to let go of the internal fight, the battle to control your environment or situation. Change the perspective.. what if this is happening for a reason? What if this is a message to change something for the better? What if this is enabling me to take the rest I need but couldn’t ask for? Soften your thoughts and let the energy flow. Hip impingement, also known as femoroacetabular impingement (FAI), occurs when the bones of the hip joint are abnormally shaped, causing them to rub against each other. This friction can lead to pain and damage over time. 🔍 Common Causes: Abnormal bone growth (Cam or Pincer deformity) Hip joint deformities High-impact activities or sports Repetitive hip movements 😣 Key Symptoms: Deep groin pain, especially after activity Limited range of motion Stiffness in the hip Sharp pain during twisting or squatting 💪 The Role of Physiotherapy: Physiotherapy can play a crucial role in managing hip impingement. Targeted exercises help to strengthen the muscles around the hip, improve flexibility, and enhance the range of motion.  With a personalised physiotherapy plan, many people experience significant reductions in pain and improvements in their ability to move without discomfort. Early diagnosis and a proactive approach, including physiotherapy, can prevent further damage and lead to better long-term outcomes! 🌟 The Sharp Physio Team Image courtesy of Complete Anatomy - Thanks to @3D4Medical  #HipPain #JointPain #HipImpingement #FAI #HipHealth #HipArthritis #HipFlexor #HipMobility #HipPainRelief #PainManagement #Orthopedics #Physiotherapy #HipReplacement #HipInjury #PhysicalTherapy #SportsInjury #JointHealth #ChronicPain #GroinPain #ArthritisRelief #HipRehab #PainAwareness #MobilityMatters #InjuryRecovery #HipStrength #PainRelief #HipSurgery #ActiveRecovery #HealthyHips #MusclePain

3 Surprising Reasons for muscles soreness ! Reason #1: Microscopic muscle tears. When you work out, especially with weights, your muscles get tiny tears. This is totally normal! As they repair, they grow back stronger—that’s how you build muscle! Reason #2: New moves. Trying a new exercise or upping your intensity? Your body isn’t used to it, so your muscles get more challenged, leading to extra soreness. "Reason #3: Inflammation. After a tough workout, your body sends more blood to the muscles for repair, causing slight inflammation. It’s part of the healing process!" Muscle soreness means progress! When you have musculoskeletal pain and dysfunction, it stands to reason you want it resolved as soon as possible right? "You fixed someone else in just one treatment, why not me? You might ask. Well the fact of the matter is that in chronic cases the pathology is far more established and will take longer to gain normal function again. When I'm assessing you and I don't see a big difference in your functional short leg, then that means there are probably multiple layers at play. The layers have piled on top of each other to make it appear like there's not a big leg length discrepancy. When I take one layer away, eg by treating your neck, (which I'll always do, even though your presenting symptom was back pain, sciatica, knee pain etc) then the short leg can become even shorter or change to the opposite leg signifying deeper layers of soft tissue dysfunction. You'll recognise this as me dorsiflexing your feet and flexing your knees at various points during the treatment. I'm looking for resolution of these layers by achieving symmetry, or to see if your body is ready to reveal the next layer while you are on the table. Maybe it will hang onto it, and slowly allow it to come to the surface while you are rehabilitating in between sessions. This is the importance of your follow up sessions. If you only attend the one treatment, there's no understanding on either of our parts about what state of equilibrium you have reached since I put the intervention in. Your body will display it's issues in the order it wants. Sometimes you will feel amazing and pain free after your treatment, and sometimes your symptoms may get worse or new ones may arise before things can settle down longer term. There is no right and wrong about it, it's unique to the individual. I firmly believe that you should also be accountable for your recovery, so I will always provide detailed aftercare advice that compliments and facilitates your healing. It's above and beyond what you need to know as part of your session, but I do this because I care about your well-being. I know what chronic pain feels like, and I am ever so grateful to the amazing therapists & teachers that have treated me over the last few years, restoring me to a pain free and fully functioning, happy and healthy life and to Tom Bowen for making it possible with his exceptional work. 🙏🙌 What makes a chronic case?
